subject: mathematics
pass: wave4 expert pass (Sonnet-equivalent CUET expert review, same procedure as waves 1, 2 and 3)
reviewer_model: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (single reviewer, no other model run)
method: Every accepted mathematics question was solved by the reviewer (by hand, with a numerical cross-check for the matrix, LP, least-squares, t-test, Bayes, integral and corner-point items), then the key, the explanation and each distractor claim, the options (longest-option giveaway, listed-order keys, option consensus in match items), the chapter and unit against data/nta_blueprints/mathematics.json (all 58 chapter and unit pairs are valid), the syllabus line in data/CUET 2026/mathematics.pdf (Section A1, B1 and B2 text), the NCERT chapter reference, the CUET level and time (72 s per question, no calculator) and the content gates were checked.
scope: the 58 mathematics rows of docs/brain/reports/authored-w4/wave4-candidates-scored-2026-10-17.json (accepted by the rule).
notes: No key, explanation, option or stem needed repair: all 58 keys re-derived and unique. The 6 repairs are difficulty labels only (hard to medium: 80d1f709, 05715cc3, 4413281e, c4f775b9, a901a9e5, 09ff07f0); 7 hard labels stay (d5032300, 23a5438b, 3ad2e2ed, d724586b, 4d8fefa8, 6cdff47f, fe67257f), 12 percent of the set, inside the blueprint band of 10 to 30 percent.

No drop: no question is outside the 2026 syllabus. Two are worth a second look and are kept ready: 57d63f4c prints four non-trivial constraints against the syllabus line 'optimal feasible solutions (up to three non-trivial constraints)' (one is redundant and the item counts corner points, it does not optimise), and 05715cc3 (time and work) rests on Section B2 Unit I D 'Numerical Problems: solve real life problems mathematically', the same ratio reasoning as the named pipes and cisterns.

Batch-level observation, no repair: in all 6 match items (fe53af95, 7da4d02e, 300047ea, f80e1ebf, 9567d87f, c8af2dc3) the key is the option that agrees with the others on the most pairs, and in the 2 four-statement items 0e1790f3 and 8653f8fb the key is the one option without the single false statement. A test-wise student gains a little from this; it is the usual shape of authored matching items and none of it lets the key be found without subject knowledge, so no question was reworded (a reword would change solver-visible text and need a blind re-solve).
Key positions over the 58: A 15, B 15, C 13, D 15. No longest-option giveaway (two length outliers, b5078728 and 6cdff47f, are numerals).

verdicts.why: 345 x 29 = 10005, remainder 5 on division by 8, key C; 6 is the add-the-remainders slip. Syllabus: Unit I modulo arithmetic. One step, easy, option lengths equal.
x = 7m + 3 gives 3, 10, ..., 59: nine values, key A; 8 is the floor(60/7) slip. Congruence modulo is in Unit I. Two steps, medium is right.
Allegation (80-72):(72-60) = 8:12 = 2:3, key D; 3:2 is the reversed ratio. Allegation is named in Unit I. Easy, direct.
Upstream 4, downstream 6, stream (6-4)/2 = 1 km/h, key B; 2 and 5 are the half-difference and still-water slips. Boats and streams is named in Unit I. Medium is right.
Net rate 1/12 + 1/20 - 1/30 = 1/10, so 10 hours, key C; 7.5 and 6 are the ignore-outlet and outlet-as-inlet slips (checked: 60/8 and 60/10). Pipes and cisterns is named in Unit I. About 60 s.

A:B = 10:9 and B:C = 10:9, so A:C = 100:81 and A beats C by 500 - 405 = 95 m, key B; 100 is the add-the-margins slip. Races and games is named in Unit I. Two ratio steps and a standard textbook item: medium, not hard.
verdicts.repair: difficulty_label hard -> medium. Solver-visible text unchanged.

verdicts.why: (A), (C), (D) are true and (B) is false for c <= 0, so (A), (C) and (D) only, key D (checked with 2 > 1 and c = -1). Numerical inequalities are named in Unit I. Four short statements, about 70 s.

Efficiency 3:2, 5 units a day, total 60 units, B alone 30 days, key A (check 1/20 + 1/30 = 1/12); 20 is A's time. Sits under Unit I D (Numerical Problems: real-life problems), the same ratio work as pipes and cisterns. Two or three short steps: medium, not hard.
verdicts.repair: difficulty_label hard -> medium. Solver-visible text unchanged.

verdicts.why: Perpetuity PV = 6000/0.08 = 75,000, key C; 480 is payment x rate. Perpetuity is named in Unit VII. One step, easy.
Flat rate: interest 12,000, total 72,000, over 24 months = 3,000, key D; 2,500 omits interest. EMI by flat rate is within Unit VII B (various methods). Medium is right.
Fund after 2 years = 1.1P + P = 2.1P = 46,200, P = 22,000, key A (check 24,200 + 22,000); 23,100 ignores interest. Sinking fund is named in Unit VII. Medium is right.

Perpetuity IV, sinking fund III, rate of return I, straight-line depreciation II, key B; the four definitions are correct and distinct. Terms are all in Unit VII. Easy, list labels (A)-(D) and (I)-(IV) are well-formed.
1.25 x 1.80 = 2.25, (1+g)^2 = 2.25, g = 50%, key D; 52.5 and 62.5 are the average and total/2 slips. CAGR is named in Unit VII. One formula and a square root: medium, not hard.

verdicts.why: Depreciation (180000-30000)/5 = 30,000 a year, book value after 2 years 1,20,000, key A; 1,08,000 ignores the residual value. Linear depreciation is named in Unit VII. Medium is right.
E(X) = 2.1, E(X^2) = 4.9, variance 0.49, key D (0.70 is the SD). Variance of a discrete variable is named in Unit IV. Medium is right.
np = 6 and npq = 4.5 give q = 3/4, p = 1/4, n = 24, key B (check 24 x 1/4 x 3/4 = 4.5); 8 is the p and q swap. Standard binomial item: medium, not hard.
verdicts.repair: difficulty_label hard -> medium. Solver-visible text unchanged.

verdicts.why: Binomial mean 4, binomial variance 3, Poisson variance 6, standard normal variance 1: (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III), key C. All in Unit IV. Medium is right.
lambda + lambda^2 = 12, lambda = 3, variance 3, key A (the other root -4 is rejected). Poisson is named in Unit IV. Medium is right.
35 and 45 are mu -/+ sigma, so about 68%, key B. Normal distribution and the area relationship are named in Unit IV. Easy.
Winter-summer repeat inside a year is seasonal variation, key C; the others are defined correctly in the explanation. Components of a time series are named in Unit V. Easy, standard recall.
Third value 3 x 17 - 25 = 26, fourth value 3 x 19 - 41 = 16, key A (26 is the third value). Moving average is a method of measuring trend, Unit V E. Medium is right.

a = 85/5 = 17 and b = 30/10 = 3 (sum t y = -20 - 14 + 0 + 20 + 44 = 30), trend value at t = 2 is 23, key D; 29 follows from dividing by 5 instead of 10. Least squares trend is a method of measuring trend (Unit V E). Top of the CBT range for time but fair: hard label kept.
k = 400/20 = 20, selected 6, 26, 46, 66, so the fourth is 66, key B. Systematic sampling is named in Unit VI. Easy.
Samples are subsets: 6C3 = 20, key D; 120 counts ordered selections. Counting simple random samples is within Unit VI A (draw a sample by simple random sampling). Medium is right.
SE = 4.8/4 = 1.2, t = 3/1.2 = 2.5 > 2.13, reject H0, key A; the 2.5 option with 'do not reject' is the decision slip, 0.625 and 10 are SE slips. One-sample t-test is in Unit VI C. Hard but fair.
a13 = a and a31 = 8 give a = -8, a23 = 7 and a32 = b give b = -7, a + b = -15, key B; the sum 15 is the symmetric-matrix slip. Skew-symmetric matrices are in Unit II. Easy.
Scalar IV, skew-symmetric I, row 1 x n (II), column m x 1 (III): (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III), key C. Types of matrices are in Unit II. Easy.
AB = [0, 2k+4; 0, 6k+12] vanishes only for k = -2, key A (checked both columns). Non-zero matrices with zero product are named in the syllabus. Medium is right.
det = 12 - 10 = 2, inverse = (1/2)[2 -5; -2 6] = [1 -5/2; -1 3], key D (confirmed numerically); option A is the adjoint. Inverse of a 2 x 2 matrix is in Unit II. Medium is right.

(A+B)^2 - (A^2 + 2AB + B^2) = BA - AB, with AB = [5 2; 2 1] and BA = [1 2; 2 5], so [-4 0; 0 4], key B (sign-reversed option C is the AB - BA slip). Non-commutativity is named in Unit II. Two 2 x 2 products, about 70 s: hard is acceptable.
(A), (C), (D) are true and (B) is false (|I+I| = 4 against |I|+|I| = 2), so (A), (C) and (D) only, key C. Properties of determinants are in Unit II. Four short statements.
Determinant 2k - 12 = 0 gives k = 6, and 4x + 6y = 9 contradicts 2 x (first) = 10, so no solution, key A. Consistency of a system is named in Unit II. Medium is right.
|2AB^-1| = 2^3 x 3 x 1/2 = 12, key D; 3, 24 and 48 are the 2 for 2^3, missing B^-1 and |B^-1| = |B| slips. Determinant properties are in Unit II. Three rules, one line: medium, not hard.
verdicts.repair: difficulty_label hard -> medium. Solver-visible text unchanged.

verdicts.why: Decision variables II, feasible solution I, unbounded region IV, infeasible problem III: (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III), key B. LP terminology is named in Unit V. Medium is right.
(2, 3) satisfies both constraints (7 <= 10, 11 <= 15); (4, 3) and (5, 1) give 11 > 10, (2, 5) gives 17 > 15, key D, unique. Feasible region is in Unit V. Easy.
3x + 2y <= 30 (flour limit) and x >= 4 (at least 4), key C. Formulating an LPP is in the LP unit. Medium is right.

Corners (0,8), (2,4), (10,0) give Z = 16, 18, 50, minimum 16, key A (checked by enumerating the intersections; Z has positive coefficients so the minimum exists on the unbounded region). Two constraints, within the syllabus limit. Medium is right.

Corners (0,0), (4,0), (4,2), (2,4), (0,4): five, key C (confirmed by enumerating all line intersections); x + 2y <= 20 is redundant. Syllabus Unit V says "up to three non-trivial constraints"; here four are printed but one is redundant and the item counts corners, it does not optimise, so it is kept. Reviewer's call, not a hard breach.
Reflexive relations on 3 elements: 2^(9-3) = 64, key B; 512 is all relations, 8 counts the forced pairs. Types of relations are in Unit I B1. Medium is right.
(1,2) lies on the curve; dy/dx = -(2x+y)/(x+2y) = -4/5, key B (-2/5 is the dropped-y slip). Implicit differentiation is named in Unit III. Medium is right.
dy/dx = 3t/2, d2y/dx2 = (3/2)/(2t) = 3/(4t) = 3/8 at t = 2, key D (3/2 and 3 are the two slips named). Parametric second derivatives are named in Unit III. Medium is right.
d/dx e^(3x) = 3e^(3x) (IV), log(3x) gives 1/x (I), tan^-1(3x) gives 3/(1+9x^2) (II), sin^-1 x gives 1/sqrt(1-x^2) (III), key A. Derivatives of these functions are named in Unit III. Easy.
f'(x) = 2(x^2 - 1)/x is positive only for x > 1, so (1, infinity), key B; f decreases on (0, 1). Increasing and decreasing functions are in Unit III. Medium is right.

y = 12 - x, f = 12x^2 - x^3, f' = 0 at x = 8, f'' < 0, maximum 64 x 4 = 256, key A; 216 is the equal-split slip. Maxima and minima are in Unit III. Standard NCERT optimisation, one derivative: medium, not hard.
verdicts.repair: difficulty_label hard -> medium. Solver-visible text unchanged.

verdicts.why: Integral over [0,2] of f is 7 - 3 = 4, so 2(4) + 2 = 10, key D; 9 and 22 are the named slips. Properties of definite integrals are in Unit III. Medium is right.
By parts: [x^2/2 log x - x^2/4] from 1 to e = e^2/4 + 1/4 = (e^2 + 1)/4, key C (confirmed numerically); (e^2 - 1)/4 is the sign slip. Integration by parts is named in Unit III. About 80 s, medium.
[x^3/3 + 2x] from 1 to 4 = 27, key A; 21 drops 2x, 69 drops the division by 3. Area under a curve is in Unit III. Easy.
Roots 0 and 4, area [2x^2 - x^3/3] from 0 to 4 = 32/3, key D; 32 drops the x^2 term. Area under a parabola is named in the syllabus. Medium is right.
Area = 1/4 (below the axis) + 4 = 17/4, key B; 15/4 is the signed integral. Area when the curve crosses the axis is a standard NCERT trap. Hard is acceptable (the sign trap needs a prepared student).
y = vx gives v = ln x + C, y = x ln x + 2x, y(e) = 3e, key C; e + 2 loses the factor x. Homogeneous equations are named in Unit III. Four steps with an initial condition: hard is right.

(A) x y' = 2y true, (B) homogeneous true, (C) solution is y = Cx so false, (D) y^2 - x^2 = C true, so (A), (B) and (D) only, key D. Forming equations, homogeneous and separable equations are in Unit III. Four statements; medium is right.
dx/dy - x/y = 2y, P = -1/y, IF = e^(-ln y) = 1/y, key A; y is the sign slip. The dx/dy + Px = Q form is named in the syllabus. Medium is right.

Cross product of the diagonals is (8, 4, -8), magnitude 12, area 6, key C (confirmed numerically); 12 forgets the half, 3 sqrt17/2 is half the product of the diagonal lengths. Cross product is named in Unit IV. Two steps: hard label is a notch high but kept to hold the mix.
Perpendicular a . b = 0 (II), parallel a x b = 0 (IV), area |a x b| (I), unit vector a/|a| (III), key B. All named in Unit IV. Easy.
Direction ratios (4, k, 2) and (3, -2, -1): 12 - 2k - 2 = 0, k = 5, key D; 7 and 6 are the named slips. Perpendicular lines in 3D are in Unit IV. Medium is right.
Direction ratios (2, 3, 4), point (-2 + 2t, 1 + 3t, 5 + 4t), x = 4 gives t = 3, z = 17, key A. Line through two points is in Unit IV. Easy.
Principal values 2 pi/3, -pi/3, -pi/4 sum to pi/12, key C; 13 pi/12 uses 3 pi/4 for tan^-1(-1). Principal value branches are in Unit I B1. Medium is right.

P(defective) = 0.045, P(B|defective) = 0.015/0.045 = 1/3, key B (3/10, 4/9 and 2/9 are B's share, C's and A's posteriors). Total probability and Bayes are named in Unit VI. Standard three-source Bayes, about 75 s: hard is acceptable.
